title: Shared spaces
titleCn: 共享空间：蒙德曼的交通理念

paragraphs.text: Hi, Tina. Shall we chat about our project? We'll need to start writing soon, so it's useful to discuss the background reading we've done.
Sure. When I first heard the term shared spaces, I didn't realize that it's just about getting rid of everything separating pedestrians and vehicles.
So that they share the space on the road.
Exactly. So there'd be no pavements, no street signs, no traffic lights. People are wanting to get rid of them.
Well, some people, like that guy in Holland.

Monderman. Yes, he's credited with starting the whole thing. So far as I can tell, one of his main aims was to create behaviors among road users which would lead to fewer accidents because drivers would be driving at a sensible speed and be more wary of pedestrians.

Right. And also, he hoped that rather than stopping and starting all the time, it would keep traffic moving more. I also think that the aesthetics of a street are improved if you get rid of traffic lights and things.
But that wasn't really his goal, even though it sounds like a good idea.

Yes. Let's think about summarizing Monderman's main ideas. Like that if there are restrictions everywhere, speed limits, no parking notices or whatever, that just makes drivers less aware of other road users and less concerned for them. [notification sound] You know, they think if they're following all the rules, [notification sound] that makes them a good driver.
Sure. He was important because he didn't accept that the status quo is necessarily a good thing. The council might have installed items of street furniture.
Like pedestrian crossings, uh, and guardrails, street lamps.
But he said you shouldn't assume that they necessarily help anyone just because they're there. And if they don't, then scrap them. I mean, their thinking may have been out of date.
